I reviewed the diff for PR #603 (report-only re-audit of PROJEXA ERP E2E) and wrote `review-verdict.json` with verdict **reject**.

Findings:
- The core deliverable — `ai-os/audits/projexa_erp_e2e_reaudit_2026-07-27.md` and the `ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml` entry — checked out well. I independently spot-verified several of its specific claims against real repo state (not just trusting the report): `computeHierarchicalAmount()`/`parentLineItemId`/`breakdownPercentage` in compliance-tracker's schema/BoQ service, and projexa's per-scope IndexedDB offline queue plus the last-owner/admin demotion guard, including the cited commit SHAs — all genuinely present.
- But `PROGRESS.md` isn't actually "report-only" as the PR's own text claims. At the merge base, `PROGRESS.md` held 281 lines of real prior-task history; this PR nets it down to 57, losing ~224 lines. The intervening "restore" commit's message claims it put back the prior tasks' notes "matching main's history," but it only reattached a stale, already-truncated 32-line fragment — not the real content. That's a self-report that doesn't match what the diff actually does, which is exactly what this review is supposed to catch, even though the underlying data isn't unrecoverable (still in git history).

No `.github/workflows/**` files are touched, so that hard rule doesn't apply here. Verdict is reject with a specific, easily-fixable ask: rebuild `PROGRESS.md` from the real `df665722` content and re-append the new section, then resubmit.
